comment: One profile per OpenStack release. A release without a profile is untested. A profile makes a release usable for changes only after a lab validation has been recorded in the journal (see profiles.py).

Queens.source: Owner's playbook v1.2, section 15 (checked against the Queens source; not yet run on a cloud)

variants.live_migration_listing: novaclient: nova server-migration-list <instance>. python-openstackclient of this era has no equivalent. An error from the command is a stop, never 'no migration'.
variants.attach_flow: to be determined in the lab (playbook test T5): old style or attachment-id style
variants.destination_helper_interpreter: the interpreter that runs cinder-volume (may be Python 2); the helper must run on Python 2 and 3

notes: Vendor builds carry patches. Lab validation must confirm the behaviour on the actual build.
Not verified in the playbook and left for the lab: attach flow, boot-from-volume swap, Purity size unit, recover-with-snapshots, scheduler 'or' operator.
Nova shows whether an instance is locked only from microversion 2.9 (the Queens maximum is 2.60); OpenMove sends 2.9 and refuses an instance whose answer has no lock state.
After a reverse migration the array may keep the real target volume only for its pending-eradication window; an explicit array copy before the record swap is needed for a longer recovery.

2025.1.source: The OpenMove lab: DevStack stable/2025.1 on the owner's machine (docs/LAB.md). Cinder 3.71 and Nova 2.100 were read from the running lab.
notes: A lab profile. It lets the engine run against the lab and nowhere else; a customer cloud on this release would still need its own recorded validation (gate G0).
The lab back-ends are LVM, not SolidFire or FlashArray, so nothing here says anything about their drivers.
